knowledge:
- key_parameters: type=Method to find the threshold (e.g., "mutinfo" for maximal mutual information) ;; prob=Quantile of within-class/between-class distances to set bounds for D (default is 0.5, set to NA to remove constraint) ;; minScore=The score cutoff (C) above which an object is classified as a member of a class (default is 0.45) ;; doffset=Small offset (d) in the denominator of the match score calculation to prevent over-weighting small groups (default is 0.5) ;; maxDepth=Maximum number of times re-partitioning may occur if classification results in confusion
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation
- when_to_use: When performing supervised classification of query objects against a reference set using pairwise distances, especially when you want to define an optimal similarity threshold distinguishing within-group from between-group comparisons and handle cases of confusion, no match, or outliers
- pitfalls: If the dataset contains some closely related classes and some distantly related classes, a single threshold D may perform poorly ;; Increasing minScore improves specificity but decreases sensitivity, potentially leading to more "no match" or "confusion" classifications ;; Small reference groups can have over-weighted match scores if doffset is not set appropriately

workflows.name: threshold_based_classification
workflows.intent: Perform supervised classification of query samples and leave-one-out cross-validation using a pairwise distance matrix and group labels.
input: groups (factor or vector of class labels for the reference objects)
dvect (vector of distances between a query object and each reference object)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate optimal separation threshold using findThreshold ;; 2. Visualize distances and threshold using plotDistances and scaleDistPlot ;; 3. Classify a query sample using classify or pull ;; 4. Print classification results using printClst ;; 5. Perform leave-one-out cross-validation using lapply and classify
workflows.code:
library(clst)
data(iris)
dmat <- as.matrix(dist(iris[,1:4], method="euclidean"))
groups <- iris$Species
ii <- c(1,125)
plot(scaleDistPlot(dmat, groups, indices=ii,O=ii))
thresh <- findThreshold(dmat, groups, type="mutinfo")
str(thresh)
thresh2 <- findThreshold(dmat, groups, type="mutinfo", prob=NA)
print(thresh2$interval)
plot(do.call(plotDistances, thresh))
plot(do.call(plotDistances, thresh2))
ind <- 1
species <- gettextf('I. %s', groups[ind])
cat('class of "unknown" sample is',species)
dmat1 <- dmat[-ind,-ind]
groups1 <- groups[-ind]
dvect1 <- dmat[ind, -ind]
cc <- classify(dmat1, groups1, dvect1)
printClst(cc)
ind <- 125
species = gettextf('I. %s', groups[ind])
pp <- pull(dmat, groups, ind)
cc <- do.call(classify, pp)
cat(paste('class of "unknown" sample is', species))
printClst(cc)
loo <- lapply(seq_along(groups), function(i){
  do.call(classify, pull(dmat, groups, i))
})
matches <- lapply(loo, function(x) rev(x)[[1]]$matches)
result <- sapply(matches, paste, collapse='-')
table(ifelse(result=='','no match',result),groups)
confusion <- sapply(matches, length) > 1
no_match <- sapply(matches, length) < 1
plot(scaleDistPlot(dmat, groups, fill=confusion, O=confusion, X=no_match))
loo <- lapply(seq_along(groups), function(i){
 do.call(classify, c(pull(dmat, groups, i),minScore=0.65))
})
matches <- lapply(loo, function(x) rev(x)[[1]]$matches)
result <- sapply(matches, paste, collapse='-')
table(ifelse(result=='','no match',result),groups)
confusion <- sapply(matches, length) > 1
no_match <- sapply(matches, length) < 1
plot(scaleDistPlot(dmat, groups, fill=confusion, O=confusion,
                    X=no_match, indices=no_match))
printClst(loo[[118]])
